run.question:
Alertmanager alert NoRequestsReceived (severity critical) is firing for service otel-demo/accounting since 2026-11-25T22:33:49Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The NoRequestsReceived alert for otel-demo/accounting is driven by a real collapse of accounting's span activity: traces_span_metrics_calls_total for service_name="accounting" falls to 0 from the 22:30:49 sample on (last non-zero 2m rate 22:29:49), and at 22:38:49 accounting is the only counted service at 0 spans/s while frontend, checkout, product-catalog, cart etc. keep normal rates. The accounting pod itself is healthy (Running/Ready, restartCount 0, container started 22:21:09, Deployment generation 1 untouched), and its deployment log shows normal order consumption until 22:28:34, then librdkafka errors "2/2 brokers are down" (22:28:28-22:28:33) and "Offset commit ... failed ... Broker: The group id does not exist: orders" at 22:28:34.09, after which the container writes nothing at all. On the dependency side, the single-broker kafka Deployment was modified at 22:28:22 by field manager OpenAPI-Generator (generation 1 to 2): the new ReplicaSet kafka-867857665f adds a nodeSelector kubernetes.io/hostname=kind-environment-worker and priorityClassName=application-non-critical, the old pod kafka-545455d985-xrs7g was deleted, the new broker finished starting at 22:28:33, all __consumer_offsets metadata loaded 0 records, and the orders topic log restarted (partition-0 offset reset from 216 to 31). Accounting rejoined group "accounting" (generation 1, 1 member) but its committed offset then froze at 215 while the topic offset advanced to 359 - i.e. it stopped consuming - while checkout kept publishing orders (~0.43 spans/s) and fraud-detection kept consuming them (~0.9 msg/s, lag reset and advancing). A second injected object, Deployment critical-data-collector (21 replicas of /bin/sh -c "sleep infinity", labels opentelemetry.io/name=kafka, priorityClassName=application-critical, created 22:28:39 by OpenAPI-Generator), now supplies 21 of the 22 endpoints behind the kafka Service, so most new connections to kafka:9092 land on pods with no listener on 9092. Checked and not implicated: accounting pod crash/OOM (restarts 0), NetworkPolicies (none exist in otel-demo), ResourceQuota (none in otel-demo), flagd fault flags (all defaultVariant "off", including kafkaQueueProblems), and error spans across all services (0 at 22:38:49). Conclusion is partial because the exact client-side reason accounting never resumes (no further log lines or connection errors after 22:28:34) and the role of the fake kafka endpoints in that stall are not directly observed, and change history is not an integrated source.

claims.text: Alert NoRequestsReceived for service accounting is firing: rule query sum by (service_name, namespace) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{namespace="otel-demo",service_name!~"flagd|load-generator|chatbot|mcp",status_code=~"STATUS_CODE_UNSET|STATUS_CODE_OK"}[5m])) == 0, duration 300s, state firing, activeAt 2026-11-25T22:33:49Z, value 0.

accounting's own span rate collapsed to zero: sum by (span_name,status_code) rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="accounting"}[2m]) is non-zero through the 22:29:49 point for receive orders / order-consumed / astronomy_db (e.g. 0.2444 at 22:29:49) and 0 at 22:30:49 and every later point through 22:38:49.

At 22:38:49 accounting is the only non-excluded service at zero span rate (0), while frontend 42.33, frontend-proxy 19.0, product-catalog 20.10, cart 14.75, checkout 7.13, load-generator 18.83, fraud-detection 1.03, payment 1.03 spans/s; chatbot and mcp are also 0 but are excluded by the alert expression.

The accounting pod accounting-7694cf945c-nfcb5 is Running and Ready with restartCount 0 (container startedAt 2026-11-25T22:21:09Z, startTime 22:20:54Z), owned by ReplicaSet accounting-7694cf945c; the accounting Deployment is still generation 1/revision 1 with a single helm Apply at 22:20:53Z, i.e. its template was not changed during the incident.

accounting consumed orders normally until 22:28:34: container logs show repeated 'info: Accounting.Consumer[...]' plus 'Order details: {...}' lines through 22:27:01 and up to 22:28:34, with no log line at all after 2026-11-25T22:28:34.09Z (newest line in the container stream).

Immediately before going silent, accounting's Kafka client logged '%3|...|ERROR|rdkafka#consumer-1| [thrd:kafka:9092...]: 2/2 brokers are down' repeatedly from 22:28:28 to 22:28:33 and then COMMITFAIL 'Offset commit (cgrp auto commit timer) failed ... Broker: The group id does not exist: orders((null))[0]@222' at 22:28:34.09Z.

The kafka Deployment was changed at 2026-11-25T22:28:22Z by field manager OpenAPI-Generator (generation 1 to 2, revision 2); ReplicaSet kafka-867857665f (created 22:28:22Z, replicas 1) replaced kafka-545455d985 (replicas 0), and a Killing event plus ReplicaSet SuccessfulDelete exist for pod kafka-545455d985-xrs7g.

The change in the kafka pod template is a scheduling change: the new ReplicaSet adds spec.template.spec.nodeSelector {kubernetes.io/hostname: kind-environment-worker} and a priorityClassName absent from the old ReplicaSet, while container image, env, ports, resources and probes are identical; the live Deployment kafka therefore carries nodeSelector kubernetes.io/hostname=kind-environment-worker and priorityClassName 'application-non-critical'. Only Deployment kafka and Deployment critical-data-collector carry priorityClassName/nodeSelector in otel-demo.

The replacement broker kafka-867857665f-glb28 (startTime 22:28:22Z, restartCount 0) reached 'Kafka Server started' at 22:28:33.558Z with all __consumer_offsets metadata partitions loading '0 records', and then warned 'Auto topic creation failed for orders with error TOPIC_ALREADY_EXISTS' at 22:28:33.780Z - i.e. the broker came up without its previous group/offset state.

Accounting did rejoin the restarted broker's group: the coordinator logged group accounting joining in Empty state, stabilizing generation 1 with 1 member and receiving an assignment at 22:28:34.094-22:28:34.101Z, and kafka_consumer_group_members{group="accounting"} stays 1 at every sample through 22:38:49.

Accounting stopped advancing its consumer offset while messages kept arriving: kafka_consumer_group_offset_sum_ratio{group="accounting",topic="orders"} climbs 11 to 215 up to 22:27:49 and is frozen at 215 at every later sample (22:28:49-22:33:49), whereas topic orders partition 0 current offset resets from 216 to 31 at 22:28:49 and then climbs 31,67,106,152,183,214,241,276,317,359 through 22:38:49.

Producers and the other consumer stayed healthy: checkout's 'publish orders' span rate stays about 0.33-0.49/s through the 22:38:49 sample, and kafka_consumer_records_consumed_total{client_id="consumer-fraud-detection-1",topic="orders"} keeps a rate of about 0.64-0.94/s with group fraud-detection offsets reset and advancing (30,65,105,151,183,213,241,274,314,359).

A second injected object exists: Deployment critical-data-collector (otel-demo) has replicas 21, container /bin/sh -c "sleep infinity" with no ports/env, labels app.kubernetes.io/component=kafka and opentelemetry.io/name=kafka, nodeSelector kind-environment-worker and priorityClassName 'application-critical', and its managedFields show an OpenAPI-Generator Update at 2026-11-25T22:28:39Z; 21 pods critical-data-collector-84899d6876-* are Running/Ready with restartCount 0, all started 22:28:39Z.

Because the kafka Service selects pods by {opentelemetry.io/name: kafka}, the 21 sleep-infinity critical-data-collector pods became endpoints of Services/kafka: the kafka Endpoints object lists 22 addresses (kafka-867857665f-glb28 plus 21 critical-data-collector-84899d6876-* pods) all mapped to targetPorts 9092/9093, so 21 of 22 endpoints have no process listening on 9092.

Checked and not implicated as causes: the flagd ConfigMap demo.flagd.json has every flag at defaultVariant "off" (including kafkaQueueProblems, whose description is 'Overloads Kafka queue while simultaneously introducing a consumer side delay leading to a lag spike'); the only NetworkPolicy in the cluster is itbench-clickhouse-ingress in itbench-observability (none in otel-demo); and there is no ResourceQuota in otel-demo.

No service shows error spans at 22:38:49 (sum by service_name of rate(...status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"[5m]) is 0 for cart, recommendation, accounting, agent, frontend, frontend-proxy, load-generator, fraud-detection, ad, flagd, payment), and accounting's pod reports Ready with 0 restarts, so neither a crash loop nor an application error burst explains the missing accounting traffic.

accounting is affected by this cause: its own receive orders / order-consumed spans went to zero, its own container logged 'The group id does not exist: orders' for its consumer group, and its group's committed offset froze at 215 while orders partition 0 advanced to 359.

Most likely causal chain: the pod-template change applied to Deployment kafka at 22:28:22Z by OpenAPI-Generator (nodeSelector + priorityClassName) replaced the single broker, and the broker came back without its previous state (all __consumer_offsets partitions loaded 0 records; orders partition-0 offset reset 216 to 31), which is exactly when accounting's client logged '2/2 brokers are down' and 'The group id does not exist: orders'; accounting then never resumed consuming (offset frozen, zero spans), producing the NoRequestsReceived condition. The exact client-side stall state after rejoining is not directly observed.

Second candidate that remains open: Deployment critical-data-collector (applied at 22:28:39Z, five seconds after accounting's last log line) injected 21 pods that match the kafka Service selector, so most new connections to kafka:9092 are routed to pods that do not listen on 9092; this would prevent accounting (or any client) from re-establishing a fetch connection and would keep the outage in place. It is not proven for accounting because accounting logs no connection or connect-timeout errors after 22:28:34Z.

Rejected: the broker restart alone is not sufficient to explain the outage, because the sibling consumer group fraud-detection went through the same restart (joining group fraud-detection at 22:28:33.98Z, offsets reset) and kept consuming orders at 0.64-0.94 msg/s with its lag series continuing through 22:38:49.

Advisory: remove or relabel the 21 critical-data-collector pods so they no longer match Services/kafka selector {opentelemetry.io/name: kafka}, verify Services/kafka endpoints reduce to the broker pod, then restart the accounting consumer pod so its group rejoins from a clean state; also review the external OpenAPI-Generator writes to the kafka Deployment (nodeSelector and priorityClassName application-non-critical) before accepting the broker as stable.

gaps: The change_history integration is not available, so the actor behind field manager OpenAPI-Generator and the reason for the kafka Deployment and critical-data-collector changes cannot be confirmed beyond managedFieldsSummary timestamps.

Accounting's container produced no log line after 22:28:34.09Z and no connect/connection-refused or session-timeout messages, so whether its consumer is stuck in the rebalance/join state, blocked in message handling, or unable to open a fetch connection could not be determined from logs.

The kafka_consumer_group_offset/lag series for group accounting stop after the 22:33:49 sample while group fraud-detection continues, so accounting's current lag cannot be read beyond 22:33:49; the reason the kafkametricsreceiver stopped reporting that group is unknown.
No direct observation of kube-proxy endpoint selection for accounting's connections, so the endpoint-pollution candidate cannot be confirmed or excluded for that pod.

PriorityClass objects (application-critical / application-non-critical) are not a readable resource kind in this run, and no eviction or preemption event for kafka was observed, so any eviction-related effect of the priority change is unknown.
Jaeger's sampled view returned accounting spans only up to 22:21:38Z (data_as_of), so no trace-level evidence exists for accounting's final, stalled order after 22:28:34Z.
next_steps: Inspect Services/kafka endpoints again after any cleanup and confirm only kafka-867857665f-glb28 remains, then restart the accounting deployment and confirm order-consumed spans and group offset advance.
Compare the kafka Deployment with the helm chart source (astronomy-shop 0.42.8) to confirm the nodeSelector and priorityClassName application-non-critical were not helm-managed settings.
Ask the platform owner which injected scenario created Deployment critical-data-collector (21 sleep replicas) and Deployment-kafka template change at 22:28:22Z/22:28:39Z.
If accounting still does not consume after endpoints are cleaned, capture a thread/consumer dump from the accounting pod to establish whether it is blocked in message handling or in group rejoin.

hypothesis.text: Most likely causal chain: the pod-template change applied to Deployment kafka at 22:28:22Z by OpenAPI-Generator (nodeSelector + priorityClassName) replaced the single broker, and the broker came back without its previous state (all __consumer_offsets partitions loaded 0 records; orders partition-0 offset reset 216 to 31), which is exactly when accounting's client logged '2/2 brokers are down' and 'The group id does not exist: orders'; accounting then never resumed consuming (offset frozen, zero spans), producing the NoRequestsReceived condition. It is not proven for accounting because accounting logs no connection or connect-timeout errors after 22:28:34Z.

recommendation.text: Advisory: remove or relabel the 21 critical-data-collector pods so they no longer match Services/kafka selector {opentelemetry.io/name: kafka}, verify Services/kafka endpoints reduce to the broker pod, then restart the accounting consumer pod so its group rejoins from a clean state; also review the external OpenAPI-Generator writes to the kafka Deployment (nodeSelector and priorityClassName application-non-critical) before accepting the broker as stable.

rejected_hypothesis.text: Rejected: the broker restart alone is not sufficient to explain the outage, because the sibling consumer group fraud-detection went through the same restart (joining group fraud-detection at 22:28:33.98Z, offsets reset) and kept consuming orders at 0.64-0.94 msg/s with its lag series continuing through 22:38:49.
